title: Pairing as a QR code: nerv open --phone --qr and Settings → Pair a device
goal: Scanning a QR opens the dashboard in Safari on a page that shows the pairing code; the owner types it in the installed app, which pairs (owner decision 2026-11-24)
acceptance: A vendored, pinned, dependency-free MIT QR encoder (named to the owner before adding)
nerv open --phone --qr prints a terminal QR plus the short code; Settings shows the same
The iOS limit (a scan opens Safari, not the installed app) is stated in the procedure

Owner decision 2026-11-24: the QR link opens the Safari dashboard on a page that displays the short pairing code (and how to open the installed app) without spending it; Safari never pairs. The code is spent only when typed in the installed app, which stores the 90-day device credential
The code travels in the URL fragment (#), never the query, so it is not sent to the server, logged or kept in the referrer; the page shows it only while unexpired

Owner clarification 2026-11-24: the QR opens the real dashboard URL with the code in the fragment; a browser tab shows the code prominently with the steps 1. Share → Add to Home Screen, 2. Open NERV from the Home Screen, 3. Type this code (valid until HH:MM); the page clears the fragment (history.replaceState) and the manifest start_url has none, so the installed app keeps no code; a code minted for a QR lasts 10 minutes (single use, same rate limits), stated in the CLI output
Owner decisions 2026-11-24: "uqr ok" (vendor uqr 0.1.3 as proposed) and "session can mint" (a dashboard session may mint pairing codes; paired devices stay 403)
privacy: Neutral fixtures only; no personal data.
escalation: A material scope or effort increase goes to the owner

effort.basis: Estimated 2026-11-23 at agent speed. Not a measurement. Closed 2026-11-24 in the reconciliation: PR #716 merged on green CI after independent security review; the iPhone check is F-118-T04.
